messages:
jules: quick heads-up: after the kernel-selection heuristic change we merged this morning, canary perf shows host-side p99 CPU for short-chat workloads up ~8%
maria: ouch. which path is burning the cycles?
jules: perf flame and hotspots point to tokenize + framer + more writev/syscall overhead. collapsed hotspot: parse::tokenize 42%, parse::framer 20%, grpc::small_write 8%, kvcache::lookup 10%, kernel_select 6%, syscalls/other 14%
cheng: tokenization jumping that much is surprising. any trace-level evidence of more fragmented frames?
jules: yes — trace t-20260308-9 shows avg frames/request for <64-token prompts increased 1.5x -> 3.2. writev count per request doubled. HTTP2 WINDOW_UPDATE pacing also appears correlated (we see more WINDOW_UPDATEs interleaved with proto reads)
samir: could kernel selection be reducing minibatch target or changing framing hints sent to preproc?
jules: exactly. new fallback to CP-constrained kernels reduces our minibatch ceiling when batch_hints low; framer now emits smaller proto slices to favor low-latency batches which prevents coalescing
maria: smallwrites raise syscall+grpc framing overhead, and small prefix fragments degrade kvcache locality. do we have numbers for kvcache tail hit-rate?
jules: tail kvcache hit-rate for tiny prompts down ~1.6% at p99; eviction churn up ~7% for small-prefix shards
cheng: hypothesis: hysteresis missing in kernel switch. we flip to CP kernel on first low-hint signal for a connection and never re-evaluate quickly -> long-lived connections stay in low-minibatch mode even when request mix fluctuates
samir: propose three short-term experiments: (A) add kernel-hold counter (hold for N requests or T ms before switch), (B) coalesce adjacent proto slices in host-preproc within a small time window (e.g., 1.5ms) for minibatch < M, (C) defensive kvcache admission tweak to accept slightly larger prefixes for recent-evict shards
maria: I like A+B as low-risk; C needs hit-rate sim and smoke tests. can we run microbench for mixed short/long traffic?
jules: I built a microbench harness: git rev: 4f9b2c3. Repro command (local replay):
```
./bench/replay --trace=short-mix.trace --env KERNEL_PREF=fallback --duration=300 --concurrency=80
```
results baseline vs fallback: p50 latency +1.2ms, p95 +11ms, p99 CPU +8% for fallback
cheng: I'll prototype kernel-hold: increment hold_counter on switch, decrement per-request; only switch if hold_counter==0. Add metric host.kernel.hold_count and expose via zap
samir: for coalesce, minimal implementation: merge consecutive proto fragments produced by framer if delta_ts <= 1.5ms and combined_size <= 8KB. Add featureflag host.ingress.coalesce_smallwrites
maria: safety net: gate coalesce on tenant opt-in and a perf rollup threshold. Also add smoke assertion: kvcache.hit_rate_drop <= 0.5% vs baseline for short prompts
jules: rollout plan: rollback kernel-selection fallback change on canary now, while A/Bing hold+coalesce on next canary group. If metrics look good, promote stable next week
ops-bot: deploy scheduled: rollback-pr #5178 -> eng-runtime-canary in 8m
samir: I'll instrument traces to capture writev_count, frames_per_req, kvcache.hit (sample 1%) and include flame snapshots in the dashboard panel host/parse/frames
cheng: will push PR with kernel-hold + coalesce prototype, include microbench harness and replay script. label: perf/host-hysteresis
maria: add smoke tests: bench asserts and kvcache regression test, and a canary runbook (how to rollback, queries to capture)
jules: thanks. once canary finishes ping here with canary-id and perf diffs. if fallback rollback reduces p99 CPU by >=6% we keep rollback and iterate on hold+coalesce
samir: noted. also suggest adding a long-tail tracer: sample 0.1% of connections but capture full per-request framing to help root-cause in future regressions
jules: agreed. thanks all :thumbsup:
